## 1. Goal
The best possible UI/UX for the website, for a viva examiner who has 3 minutes to understand an online two-resource scheduler, and for Krishna, who must demo it without a hitch (PRD §10A). The engine's decisions, numbers and log sentences are shown unchanged.

## 2. Background
Krishna approved a rule change (D76): frontend frameworks, libraries, ES modules, a build tool and self-hosted web fonts are allowed when they improve the result, and Impeccable (`PRODUCT.md`, `DESIGN.md`) is the design authority. `docs/design/APPLE_DESIGN.md` is reference only.

Still fixed: scheduling logic only in `core/` (the UI calls the existing WebAssembly exports); the built site works offline from `file://` (everything bundled, fonts self-hosted, no CDN or network call); no raw HTML injection (`innerHTML`, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `v-html`), no `eval`; URL hash size-limited and parsed in `try/catch`; CSV ≤ 1 MB, every field validated, bad rows listed; loading, empty and error states; light and dark; WCAG AA; full keyboard use; reduced motion; colour never the only signal; versions verified on the official registry, lockfile committed; no build output committed; PRD §5 untouched.

## 3. Scope
**In scope:** the docs rule change; PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md (Impeccable); ranked findings; a frontend build (`make web`) in CI with an offline check; Build, Run and Compare redesigned to the direction; audit, polish and a final DESIGN.md from the shipped site.

**Out of scope:** any engine or WebAssembly export change; PRD §5; new scheduling features.

## 5. Specification
`make web` installs from the lockfile and writes the built site to a git-ignored folder; the built `index.html` opens from `file://` with the network off. Every dependency has its own D-row with the version verified on its registry.

## 6. Step-by-step tasks
1. PR 1: docs and rule change. 2. PR 2: PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md direction, ranked findings. 3. PR 3: build scaffold, CI, offline check, existing UI ported unchanged. 4. PR 4 to 6: Build, Run, Compare. 5. PR 7: audit, polish, documenter pass.

## 8. Acceptance criteria (Done when)
- [ ] Every accepted finding fixed or deferred with a reason
- [ ] Contrast, layout and offline rehearsal checks pass; `make test`, `make sanitize`, `pytest tests/py` and CI (with the frontend build) green
- [ ] The demo path runs keyboard-only from the offline `file://` build with no console errors, in light and dark
- [ ] Before and after screenshots committed
- [ ] PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md match the shipped site
- [ ] Each PR explains every library chosen and why

## 9. How to verify
`make wasm && make web`; open the built `index.html` from disk with networking off; run the checks in section 7.

## 10. Viva notes
Every library is named in DECISIONS.md with the reason it was chosen. Examiner question: "Does the website decide anything?" No: it only calls the C engine through the WebAssembly exports and shows what it returns.

## 11. Pitfalls
- ES modules do not load from `file://`: the build must inline them
- A CDN or font request that silently breaks offline
- Rewording engine sentences
